successCriteria.description: The leave-balance module exports an ILeaveBalanceService interface declaring all six operations: getBalancesForEmployee, initializeBalancesForEmployee, getAvailableBalance, reserveDays, finalizeDeduction, releaseReservation — with getAvailableBalance returning Promise<number> (async, matching the established tested contract).

initializeBalancesForEmployee fetches active policies via the policy service, calls calculateEntitlement per policy using hireDate.getFullYear() as the fiscal year, and persists all balances in a single createBatch call with usedDays=0, pendingDays=0, status='ACTIVE'; returns [] when no active policies exist.

reserveDays computes available = remainingDays - pendingDays and rejects with a typed INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE error when available < days, performing NO balance mutation on rejection; it increments pendingDays only when the sufficiency check passes.

finalizeDeduction atomically decrements pendingDays (floored at 0) and increments usedDays in a single repository update call; releaseReservation decrements pendingDays (floored at 0) without touching usedDays.
getAvailableBalance, reserveDays, finalizeDeduction, and releaseReservation each throw a typed NOT_FOUND error when no balance record exists for the given employee/policy/fiscal-year triple.

The leave-balance barrel (index.ts) re-exports ILeaveBalanceService and LeaveBalanceService alongside the existing Phase 4 exports, so downstream consumers (Phase 10 LeaveRequestService) import them through the module boundary.

Jest unit tests in tests/unit/modules/leave-balance/ cover reservation success, insufficient-balance rejection with no mutation, deduction (pending→used) atomicity, release (pending decrement, used untouched), non-negative pendingDays floor, NOT_FOUND on missing balance, and initializeBalancesForEmployee batch creation + empty-policies case.

constraints: Cross-module imports to leave-policy (ILeavePolicyService and AppError) must go through the leave-policy barrel (../leave-policy index.ts), never from internal files — per the module-boundary rule in ARCHITECTURE.md and AGENTS.md.
No use of any — use unknown with type guards instead (HARNESS.json no-any rule, severity high); strict TypeScript with strict null checks must pass tsc --noEmit.
All database access goes through the injected ILeaveBalanceRepository; the service must not issue SQL or touch the pg Pool directly (GP-001 / no-direct-db-outside-repository).
getAvailableBalance must remain async (Promise<number>); changing it to a synchronous number return would break the established tested contract and the Phase 10 LeaveRequestService consumer.
The service must reuse the AppError class exported from the leave-policy module for all domain errors (NOT_FOUND, INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE) rather than introducing a new error type.
outOfScope: Leave-balance HTTP routes/controllers and RBAC guards — this phase produces only the service interface and implementation; route wiring is a later phase.

Audit record creation for balance mutations — GP-002 audit wiring for reserve/finalize/release is deferred to the Phase 10 LeaveRequestService orchestration that owns the transaction unit of work; this service performs balance arithmetic only.

Transaction (PoolClient) ownership — the service relies on the repository's default shared pool; explicit BEGIN/COMMIT transaction management for the approval flow is owned by the Phase 10 LeaveRequestService, not this service.
Year-end rollover, carryover, and accrual scheduling — the reconciled architecture specifies use-it-or-lose-it with no carryover; accrual jobs are out of scope for this phase.

entityInvariants.invariant: remainingDays is a computed read-time value equal to totalEntitlement - usedDays - pendingDays; the service must never write remainingDays directly — it is derived by the repository mapper, so mutations operate only on usedDays and pendingDays.
pendingDays must never be driven below zero — finalizeDeduction and releaseReservation apply a Math.max(0, pendingDays - days) floor on every decrement.

A balance row is uniquely scoped by the (employeeId, policyId, fiscalYear) triple; every service operation that needs a single balance looks it up via findByEmployeeIdAndPolicyId with that triple and throws NOT_FOUND when absent.
Newly initialized balances start with usedDays=0, pendingDays=0, status='ACTIVE', and totalEntitlement set to the policy service's calculateEntitlement result for the hire date's fiscal year.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Delegates to findByEmployeeId when fiscalYear is omitted, or findByEmployeeIdAndFiscalYear when provided; returns [] when none exist; propagates repository errors.
Returns [] when no active policies exist (no createBatch call); otherwise persists all balances in a single createBatch. Propagates policy-service and repository errors.
Throws AppError code NOT_FOUND when no balance record exists; otherwise returns remainingDays - pendingDays.

Throws AppError NOT_FOUND when balance absent; throws AppError INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE when (remainingDays - pendingDays) < days and performs NO repository update on that failure path; otherwise increments pendingDays via a single update.
Throws AppError NOT_FOUND when balance absent; otherwise performs a single atomic update that decrements pendingDays (floored at 0) and increments usedDays by the same days amount.
Throws AppError NOT_FOUND when balance absent; otherwise performs a single update that decrements pendingDays (floored at 0) and does not modify usedDays.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The service must operate on the Phase 4 LeaveBalance model shape (id, employeeId, policyId, totalEntitlement, usedDays, pendingDays, remainingDays, fiscalYear, status, createdAt, updatedAt) and must not redefine or diverge from it.

The service must use only the ILeaveBalanceRepository methods declared in Phase 4 (findByEmployeeId, findByEmployeeIdAndFiscalYear, findByEmployeeIdAndPolicyId, create, update, createBatch) and the CreateLeaveBalanceDto/UpdateLeaveBalanceDto shapes; it must not assume repository methods that do not exist there.

The service must call ILeavePolicyService.getActivePolicies() and the synchronous calculateEntitlement(policy, hireDate, fiscalYear): number exactly as declared in Phase 8; it must not invent additional policy-service methods or alter the calculateEntitlement signature.

AppError and ILeavePolicyService must be imported from the leave-policy barrel (../leave-policy), matching the existing re-exports of AppError and ILeavePolicyService there; no direct import from leave-policy.service.ts or leave-policy.service.interface.ts.

The barrel must re-export ILeaveBalanceService and LeaveBalanceService in addition to the existing Phase 4 exports (LeaveBalance, ILeaveBalanceRepository, CreateLeaveBalanceDto, UpdateLeaveBalanceDto, LeaveBalanceRepository) without removing any of them.

The service behavior must match the ARCHITECTURE.md Implementation Notes for LeaveBalanceService: getBalancesForEmployee delegation, initializeBalancesForEmployee batch creation with hireDate.getFullYear(), getAvailableBalance returning remainingDays - pendingDays with NOT_FOUND, reserveDays sufficiency check with INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE and no mutation on failure, finalizeDeduction atomic pending→used, releaseReservation pending decrement with Math.max(0,...) floor.

integrationPoints.why: initializeBalancesForEmployee depends on getActivePolicies() to enumerate active policies and calculateEntitlement() to compute each balance's totalEntitlement; AppError is reused for typed domain errors.
All balance persistence and lookups (findByEmployeeIdAndPolicyId, findByEmployeeId/AndFiscalYear, update, createBatch) flow through this injected repository per GP-001.

Phase 10 consumes ILeaveBalanceService — calling getAvailableBalance for the sufficiency check, reserveDays on submit, finalizeDeduction on approve, and releaseReservation on reject/cancel — so the async signatures and error codes here are the binding contract for that consumer.
